Exploring Private 5G Networks Through the Lens of MNOs
GSMA OnGo Alliance
TLDR An operator-side playbook for deploying Private 5G: requirements, the case for slicing, virtualization and edge computing, plus a step-by-step deployment guide. It frames Private 5G through MNO economics and operating models — how the operator captures value, and where the deployment pain points actually are.
Why read it A counterweight to vendor whitepapers. It matters when designing slice management, because the operator’s operating model constrains what the management plane can assume.
#private-5g · #slicing · #mno


5G Core Operator Survey — 2025 Edition: Scaling 5G SA
Mavenir
TLDR An operator survey on the services, infrastructure, and operating models driving the scaling of Standalone 5G core networks. Useful less for the conclusions than for the data: what operators are actually standardizing, where they are stuck, and which services justify the CAPEX.
Why read it A grounded view of what packet-core operators are actually shipping — a reality-check for the slice-management thesis.
#packet-core · #5g-sa · #operator


How AI-Powered Digital Twins Are Driving Autonomous Telco Networks
Amdocs
TLDR Digital twins as a risk-free sandbox for telcos: what-if testing of network changes, predictive optimization, and the path toward autonomous network operations. A vendor framing of the digital-twin + AI management loop — twin as the safe space where the AI proposes and the network disposes.
Why read it A concrete vendor framing of the loop that sits at the core of your research direction.
#digital-twin · #autonomous-networks · #ai


Network Digital Twin: Concepts and Reference Architecture
IETF · IRTF
TLDR An IRTF working draft defining the concepts and reference architecture for network digital twins — the vocabulary, the layering, and the boundary between the physical network and its digital counterpart, as the standards track sees it.
Why read it The standards-track definition of the exact concept under study. Worth reading for the vocabulary and layering it proposes, even if you disagree with parts of it.
#digital-twin · #standards

RFC 9889: A Realization of Network Slices for 5G Networks Using Current IP/MPLS Technologies
IETF · RFC
TLDR The first RFC that specifies how to realize 5G network slices on existing IP/MPLS transport. It maps the 3GPP slice construct onto the fabric operators already run — service chaining, EVPN, segment routing — and lays out how a slice request flows from the core down to the transport plane. It is the reference for what “a slice” concretely means when it hits the network, rather than staying a core-side abstraction.
Why read it A rare IETF/3GPP convergence artifact. Directly relevant to slice management and Private 5G over existing fabrics — worth reading before designing any slice-management plane.
#private-5g · #slicing · #ip-mpls


A Network Digital Twin of a 5G Private Network
arXiv
TLDR A full digital twin of a 5G private network — RAN plus core — covering data collection, device control, and the mapping of physical elements to their digital counterparts. Notable because it treats the whole network (not just the RAN) as the twin, and walks through the synchronization and control loops that keep the twin faithful.
Why read it Exactly at the intersection: Private 5G + digital twins + network intelligence. A concrete reference architecture to critique.
#digital-twin · #private-5g


AI-Native Network Digital Twin for Intelligent Network Management
arXiv
TLDR Proposes an AI-native network digital twin for intelligent network management in the 5G → 6G transition. The key claim: the twin is not just a simulation sandbox, but the substrate on which the management and optimization AI runs — perception, prediction, and closed-loop control all operate through the twin.
Why read it The “intelligent network management” axis of your thesis, condensed into one paper.
#digital-twin · #network-management · #6g


Ollama
Ollama
TLDR The de-facto local LLM runtime: pull and serve models with one command, with a simple OpenAI-compatible API on top. It wraps llama.cpp, so it inherits the GGML quantization story that makes 7B+ models runnable on a laptop or an edge box.
Why read it The fastest way to stand up a local inference stack for edge experiments.
#edge-inference · #local-llm

Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
arXiv · DeepMind
TLDR A foundation model that turns a single image into an interactive, steerable world — it generates plausible next frames in response to actions, rather than just predicting forward. It is the first general-purpose “world model” that can be played, and the template for how DeepMind frames world modeling as a pretraining objective.
Why read it The canonical recent reference for world models. A useful contrast to how “world models” are framed in telecom/6G literature — the word means very different things in the two fields.
#world-models · #deepmind


World Labs
World Labs
TLDR Fei-Fei Li’s “spatial intelligence” lab — building generative models that produce rich, interactive 3D worlds instead of flat images or text. The bet is that understanding space (geometry, physics, persistence) is the next frontier after language.
Why read it A signal of where world models are heading commercially — beyond text into spatial and physical simulation.
#world-models · #spatial-intelligence


Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models Into Concepts
Anthropic
TLDR Uses sparse autoencoders to decompose LLM activations into thousands of interpretable, mostly single-concept features. This is the paper that kicked off the modern interpretability wave — and the methodological template (SAE + feature analysis) that most follow-up work builds on.
Why read it Foundational for mechanistic interpretability. The feature-decomposition lens maps well onto asking “what is the network actually doing” in slice management.
#interpretability · #llm


llama.cpp
GitHub
TLDR A minimal C/C++ runtime for LLM inference on CPUs and consumer hardware — the engine behind most local inference stacks. Its GGML quantization formats are what make 7B+ models runnable on a laptop or an edge box, with no GPU required.
Why read it The practical foundation for local/edge inference experiments. Skim the README and quantization docs to ground edge-inference thinking.
#edge-inference · #local-llm
